diagnosis.root_cause: The test asserted authority_revalidated=True for an effectful action (commit) under a G3_PR scope with no executable approval. The production code at commit 68b45bd (SCRUM-674) deliberately fails closed on REQUIRE_APPROVAL: the canonical authority boundary evaluator is authority-negative and only ALLOW_PREPARATION is non-blocking. The test was written against the pre-68b45bd semantics and drifted from the live source contract.
diagnosis.source_of_truth: commit 68b45bd fix(SCRUM-674): fail closed on approval-required authority decisions — _revalidate_authority now returns allowed = (decision == 'ALLOW_PREPARATION') only; executor raises on any other verdict.

repair.change: Replaced the single drifted assertion with two tests: (1) test_authority_revalidation_invokes_real_validator_and_fails_closed_on_effectful_action — effectful commit under G3_PR with no executable approval now expects PlanBoundRuntimeError matching 'authority revalidation failed: AUTHORITY_APPROVAL_REQUIRED'; (2) test_authority_revalidation_allows_read_only_when_validator_permits — read-only inspect under G2_EXECUTION scope returns authority_revalidated=True, proving the canonical validator is actually invoked rather than skipped.
